title: Nancy Hanks Saloon, Big 25 and its piano players
summary: The Nancy Hanks and Big 25 at Iberville and Franklin, prostitutes and gamblers, and pianists Burnell Santiago, his brother Cooney, and Papa Yell; a question about a 1913 killing.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You remember the Nancy Hanks? The what? Nancy Hanks Saloon. That was on Everville though. That was on the other side of the canal.
Yeah, that was on Iperville. In Moray. Yeah, yeah. Iperville in Franklin, wasn't it?
No, that was... No, it wasn't.
That's right. You're right. Yeah, yeah. That's right. It was on Iperville in Moray.
You remember anything about that?
Huh?
You remember anything about the Nancy Hanks?

Well, yes. I remember about that. I used to come down to that. I mean, a lot of prostitutes and so on used to be around now. Yeah, well, Ada Hayes ran and she was a madam. She was a barmaid too. Yeah, that was another tough spot. And that big 25, Iperville in Franklin. That's the place where all the big gamins are going. That's why they called it big 25, right at Iperville in Franklin. They tore that place down as a big parking lot now. Well, they had a piano in there too. A lot of all those musicians when they get off down off Bourbon Street, they all wind up and beat 25. They all had a private booth there and kept a good piano in there. And all the guys coming in there and playing. Steve Lewis, drive them down. And Stone the Weather, that's before his town. This boy, Bonnell Snagel, a good piano player, the boy that died, Bonnell. And Cooney, his brother Cooney. And little, what do you call him? Papa Yell, Little Toot. Little Yell, they call him. All them fellas. Which one?
Which one is Brunnell's brother Cooney? Cooney, Cooney.
That's right. Cooney played nice piano himself. I think the both of them died.
I know his brother, they call him Black Lester.
Well, he has one brother called Cooney. I didn't know him.
You didn't know him, huh?

I know there's a mess out of him. Nice piano player. In fact, all of them is good piano players. But I believe this boy died, Cooney. And you know Bonnell died. He died in the Flint Goodrich's Hospital.
Well, I heard about how he died.
Yeah, you heard about how he killed him, huh? Uh-huh.
How about, uh, you remember the killing in the 101 Ranch or in the Tuxedo down there when they killed Billy Phillips? The Jip the Blood was in it?

Well, I came along, I came along a few years later. I know about it, but I can't remember it. About the Jip the Blood and all that stuff down there. About killing the chief and all the guys. Killing the chief was in 1895.
They killed Jip, I mean Jip the Blood killed Billy Phillips in about 1913.
Yeah, they used to make them Italian and say, how are you killing the chief? You tell them that, well you just had some trouble on hand. Well we still got plenty of tape.
